Olivia Chen: Heads up — terraform apply in staging is failing when creating the k8s secret for feature/notifications. Error shows an invalid base64 value for the token key.
Samir Patel: Can you paste the resource block?
Olivia Chen: Sure — here's the resource from the branch: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_secret" "notify" {
  metadata {
    name      = "notify-secret"
    namespace = var.namespace
  }
  data = {
    token = var.notify_token
  }
}
```
Rajiv Kumar: Looks like you're using `data` which expects base64-encoded values. If `var.notify_token` is a plain token string, either base64encode it in TF or switch to `string_data`. Provider versions differ here.
Samir Patel: Quick options:
- Change to `string_data = { token = var.notify_token }` (provider will handle encoding)
- Or keep `data` and use `token = base64encode(var.notify_token)`
- If the secret already exists in the cluster with a different format, import it first or taint.
Maya Lopez: FYI we recently merged a change (PR#423) that turned `notify_token` into a sensitive map and updated some code paths — that might have unintentionally flipped to `data` in the refactor.
Olivia Chen: Ah that explains it. I switched the resource to `string_data` locally and re-ran plan — plan looks good now.
Samir Patel: If you already applied a partial run and tfstate thinks the secret exists with the old shape, do: 
```bash
# mark for replace
terraform taint kubernetes_secret.notify
terraform apply -auto-approve
# or import the existing resource and then update
terraform import kubernetes_secret.notify staging/notify-secret
```
Olivia Chen: I tainted and applied after changing to `string_data` and it succeeded. Staging now reports the secret in `stringData` form.
Rajiv Kumar: One more gotcha — if someone created the secret manually with non-base64 in `data` or used `binaryData`, the provider may error until the cluster secret is in the expected format. If you hit that, importing the existing secret then doing a `kubectl edit` to normalize can help.
infra-bot: Detected failed apply run for workspace `staging` (run id: run-2024-04-02-10-23) — error: invalid base64 value for key 'token'.
Maya Lopez: Thanks for the quick fix, @Olivia — can you link the PR when you have a sec so I can review the refactor that introduced the switch? :thumbsup:
Olivia Chen: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/527 — includes switching to `string_data` + changelog note.
Samir Patel: Marking this one solved. If we see this again, let's add a short note in the Terraform style guide: prefer `string_data` for plain secrets unless you intentionally manage base64 yourself. :memo:
Olivia Chen: Agreed — I'll add that to the infra docs later today.
__notes: This Slack thread captures an eng-infra troubleshooting convo about Terraform k8s secret base64 errors, quick fixes (string_data vs data), taint/import commands, and a PR link. Messages are short and in-order to mimic real Slack threads.
